issues.description: Nil-guard boilerplate is copy-pasted across ~15 accessors instead of one helper or zero-valued backing struct.
issues.detail: Every accessor opens with `var slice X; if f != nil { slice = ... }`. The same special case repeats ~15 times in ir_file.go and ir_type.go. Extract a safeSlice helper, give *File/*imports a method returning safe slices, or use a zero-valued sentinel so the decision lives in one place instead of fifteen.

issues.description: Reflection-driven TestZero is fragile: treats any no-arg method as a pure accessor and encodes spec as named exceptions.
issues.detail: testZeroAny iterates NumMethod() and calls anything with NumIn()==1, which will invoke mutators or side-effecting methods if added later. Special cases for ValueNodeIndex(-1) and Context smuggle the spec into the harness. A boring table of (method, expected) per type would state intent clearly and catch real regressions.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex returns -1 sentinel for zero, conflating 'no element' with a real index value.
issues.detail: Element.ValueNodeIndex now returns -1 for the zero value, documented only in a comment. Every caller must know the magic number. (int, bool) or an Option-shaped result would separate 'is there an index' from 'what is it' and remove the named exception in the reflection harness.

issues.description: Transitive() unconditionally drops the last entry assuming descriptor.proto is implicit, without stating the invariant.
issues.detail: ir_imports.go uses `files[:max(0, len(i.files)-1)]` with a comment 'Exclude the implicit descriptor.proto.' No invariant proves the last element is always descriptor.proto. If the assumption fails, this silently drops a legitimate transitive import. State the invariant or check explicitly.

issues.description: Symbol.RawData zero-guard lives in export_test.go, hiding whether the real Raw() is nil-safe.
issues.detail: Symbol.RawData in the test-only export file guards IsZero and returns arena.Nil(). If production callers can hold zero Symbols, the guard belongs on the real accessor; if they cannot, the test does not need it. Either way, placement obscures whether zero-Symbol is supported.

issues.description: Test addition and ~15 production fixes mashed into one commit, harming bisectability.
issues.detail: The reflection test discovered the panics, but the diff lands the test and all production fixes together with no per-fix commit explaining which method panicked and why. If one fix regresses later, bisect lands on a 400-line commit. Split: one commit per logical fix, then the test on top.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR does a useful thing — hardening zero-value safety across the ir package — but lands as a fat diff that encodes the wrong shape. The dominant complaint, flagged by all three reviewers, is that the same nil-guard boilerplate is copy-pasted across ~15 accessors instead of being collapsed into one helper or a zero-valued backing struct, complecting identity with value access. The reflection-driven TestZero is fragile and smuggles the spec into named exceptions rather than stating it in a table. ValueNodeIndex's -1 sentinel is a magic value where (int, bool) belongs. Secondary concerns: an unstated invariant in Transitive() and a misplaced zero-guard in export_test.go. Needs-work, not block-merge.
